name: Irish republicanism
summary: Irish republicanism seeks a sovereign, independent, democratic Irish republic, free of British rule and of the monarchy, and traditionally a single state for the whole island. It descends from Wolfe Tone and the United Irishmen's aim of uniting Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter, and the 1916 Proclamation guaranteeing equal rights to all. It has combined armed struggle and electoral politics, and ranges from nationalist to socialist strands.
scope: The mainstream Irish republican tradition as stated in the 1916 Proclamation and the 1919 Democratic Programme, plus the modern constitutional republicanism of Sinn Féin. Dissident and legitimist strands that reject the Good Friday Agreement and the Dáil are noted but not the basis. Many answers on issues not historically addressed are inferred at low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Wolfe Tone
keyFigures.role: Founder of the United Irishmen and the figure usually named as the founder of Irish republicanism.

keyFigures.name: James Connolly
keyFigures.role: Socialist republican, signatory of the Proclamation and model for republican socialists.

keyFigures.name: Patrick Pearse
keyFigures.role: Signatory of the 1916 Proclamation and leader of the Easter Rising.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Sinn Féin proposes an all-Ireland health service modelled on the NHS.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Democratic Programme said private property must be subordinated to the public right and welfare.

cut-welfare.rationale: The Democratic Programme committed to replacing the Poor Law with a native relief scheme, and Sinn Féin proposes expanded services.

worker-ownership.rationale: The Democratic Programme favoured industry on co-operative lines and Sinn Féin proposes a worker co-operative fund.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No documented republican position; adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No documented core position; adherents are split.

state-harmful.rationale: Republicans seek to establish a sovereign state, the Republic proclaimed in 1916.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position; the tradition values armed volunteers but modern parties are split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Sinn Féin pledged to extend same-sex marriage to Northern Ireland.

abortion-legal.rationale: Sinn Féin campaigned for Yes in 2018 and committed to abortion up to 12 weeks.

more-religion-public.rationale: Republicans have a long-standing hostility with the Catholic hierarchy and stress religious liberty.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No documented position; adherents are split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Young Ireland and later republicans promoted Irish history and language as part of the national cause.

gradual-change.rationale: The tradition is defined by rebellion against the existing order, though modern parties pursue gradual constitutional change.

nation-first.rationale: Strong on national sovereignty but also internationalist and anti-imperial; adherents split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Republicanism arose from armed uprisings from Tone and Emmet to 1916, and the Proclamation justifies armed assertion of national freedom.

central-planning.rationale: The Democratic Programme favoured co-operative industry and regulation, not full central planning.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Democratic Programme aimed to develop national resources and industry in the people's interest.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Mainstream republicans do not seek to abolish money or wages.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Proclamation promises a government elected by all men and women, and the Fenian oath called for a Democratic Republic.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The republic is the defining aim, in opposition to the British Crown.

democracy-best.rationale: The Proclamation calls for a government elected by the suffrages of all men and women.

direct-votes.rationale: Republicans favour referendums on unity, but no general position on direct legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: Mainstream republicans work through parliaments and elections.

right-to-secede.rationale: Republicans want the people of Ireland to determine their own status, including leaving the UK; unionist views differ.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees equal rights and opportunities to all citizens.

political-violence-never.rationale: The movement has historically justified armed struggle, and dissident strands still do, though the mainstream now pursues peaceful means.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees religious liberty and republicans have long clashed with the Catholic hierarchy.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Proclamation promises religious and civil liberty to all, and Emmet said the war was not against any sect.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The United Irishmen sought to unite Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter, and the Proclamation cherishes all children of the nation equally.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Republicans are divided between socialist republicans following Connolly and those who put national aims first.

restore-past-order.rationale: Republicans seek a new republic rather than restoring an old order, though legitimists invoke the 1916 mandate.

direct-action.rationale: Mainstream republicans combine elections with abstentionism; direct action is characteristic only of dissident strands.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist republicans agree; nationalist strands do not.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Republicans seek an elected democratic republic.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist republicans agree; others do not.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Republicans assert national rights as well as individual rights.

national-rebirth.rationale: 1916 rebels framed the Rising partly as national renewal, but this is not a general republican position.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Republicans claim the island only, and oppose imperial expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Republicanism rests on popular sovereignty and equal citizenship, the opposite of lordly loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Contradicts the equal rights promised by the Proclamation.

revive-national-language.rationale: Young Ireland sought to revive Irish and Sinn Féin backs an Irish Language Bill.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Proclamation asserts the sovereign right of the people of Ireland to the ownership of Ireland.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Enlightenment roots but the 1916 Proclamation invokes God; split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Republicans put great weight on national history and culture.

workers-nation.rationale: Connolly combined national and class organisation; contested.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Proclamation promises equal rights to men and women.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contrary to the equal rights in the Proclamation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist republicans agree; others do not.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claim with no basis in republicanism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Democratic Programme and Sinn Féin both call for an active welfare state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees equal rights and equal opportunities to all citizens and cherishes all children equally.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Contrary to religious liberty in the Proclamation.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Proclamation grounds the republic on the sovereignty of the people.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to equal rights in the Proclamation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Republicans have themselves been banned and abstain from the state's institutions.

vanguard-party.rationale: Mainstream republicans are electoral, though dissident groups have vanguard traits.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Democratic Programme prioritised children, the aged and the poor.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Programme attributes poverty to social arrangements, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: United Irishmen aimed to unite different religions in one identity.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The Programme called for regulating food and essentials in the people's interest.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sinn Féin is soft Eurosceptic, opposes a European superstate and stresses sovereignty.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Republicans have a long-standing hostility to the Catholic hierarchy.

clerical-rule.rationale: Contrary to religious liberty and republican secularism.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Connolly opposed WWI but republicans oppose the British state; not a general position.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Sinn Féin proposes rent controls and social housing, not a ban on renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Irish Volunteers were a citizen force but modern parties do not call for abolishing professional armies.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Republicanism has justified initiating armed force against British rule, though modern constitutional strands avoid it.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Opposition to the partition of Ireland and the aim of a single Irish state is the defining republican position, shared by moderates and dissidents.

minority-language-support.rationale: Sinn Féin backs an Irish Language Act giving Irish the status Welsh has in Wales, and more Irish-language teaching in Northern Ireland.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees religious and civil liberty to all; an inference that exemptions for minority practice are accepted.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Democratic Programme ties national freedom to the nation's ownership of its resources and social justice.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees civil and religious liberty and equal rights, and republicans oppose curbing freedoms for the economy.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Republicans claim the whole island as the national territory and reject partition, but the tradition has accepted a negotiated settlement with a consent principle.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Democratic Programme says the nation's right to the land is superior to all private right and property.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The republican aim is an end to British rule in the north and the reunification of Ireland, regarding partition as imposed without consent of the Irish nation.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Republicans reject the monarchy and favour a republic, and Ireland's president is a non-partisan figurehead; the Proclamation's unity of Irish people is the model.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The republican tradition rejects monarchy and holds that sovereignty rests with the people, as the 1916 Proclamation states.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Republicanism rests on popular sovereignty and constitutional law; the Proclamation and Programme place power in the people, not above the law.

leader-cult.rationale: Republicanism stresses equal citizenship and rejects monarchical or personal glorification of rulers.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Mainstream republicanism is nationalist; only its socialist strand speaks of class struggle, and not about socialist-state restoration.

land-redistribution.rationale: The 1916 Proclamation asserts the people's ownership of Ireland, and the Land League tradition and the 1919 Democratic Programme backed land for the people.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Traditional republicanism claims the whole island of Ireland as one state, partly on the basis of the people of Ireland living across the border; it cites territory, not just nationality.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees religious and civil liberty to all citizens and Wolfe Tone sought to unite Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter.

women-must-cover.rationale: Republicanism guarantees equal rights and has no tradition of dress mandates.

common-currency.rationale: Sinn Féin has shifted between accepting the euro in Ireland and doubts about it; republicans are split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Republicanism seeks unity of the Irish across the island, but it does not call for union with other Celtic peoples; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Republican strategy and Sinn Féin's civil-rights campaign in the North fought for equal rights where Catholics live, rather than emigration.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The mainstream tradition stresses national sovereignty and the people's will over economic determinism; only the socialist strand leans to materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The 1919 Democratic Programme speaks of subordinating private property to the public good but not of competition law; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Republicanism asserts the sovereignty of the people, but modern republicans accept constitutional limits; split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees equal rights and opportunities to men and women, and Sinn Féin has adopted gender quotas for its candidates.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not a republican theme; the movement has not tried to replace material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Republican tradition, from the 1916 Rising to the IRA, holds that a small armed vanguard can start a national revolution, though constitutional republicans have since moved away.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Republicanism rejects the monarchy and aristocracy, and the Proclamation proclaims the Republic and equal rights for all citizens.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Republicanism is founded on rejecting British rule over Ireland and the sovereignty of the Irish people.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees equal rights and religious liberty to all citizens.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Republicans reject the partition of Ireland imposed by the 1920-21 settlement without the consent of the Irish nation.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Proclamation declares a Republic with a government elected by the suffrage of all men and women.

minority-veto.rationale: Sinn Féin rejects a unionist veto over Irish unity, favouring majority decision across the island.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The tradition from the United Irishmen to 1916 justifies rebellion against unlawful or illegitimate rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Republicans make the elected Dáil sovereign and reject the Crown's authority.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Democratic Programme frames welfare as a right of citizens, not charity from the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The tradition is activist and demands civic engagement.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees equal rights and opportunities to all citizens, without regard to origin.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Republicans seek an end to partition, but they frame the north as part of one undivided nation, not as territory lost to a neighbour in war.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The Proclamation and the United Irish tradition unite Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter as equal citizens.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Republicans seek a liberal democratic republic modelled on universal principles.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Mainstream republicanism accepts civilian control; only legitimist strands claim army-council authority.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The republican tradition favours representative government of an elected Dáil and parties; delegates bound to constituents is not a principle of it.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The 1919 Democratic Programme declares the nation's soil belongs to the nation and private ownership is subordinate to the public right.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The 1916 Proclamation declares the sovereignty of the people and a freely elected government, and the republic is built on an elected parliament, the Dáil.

single-official-language.rationale: Republicans revived Irish and value it, but Sinn Féin supports Irish language rights alongside English; modern adherents back bilingual rather than sole-language policy.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Republicanism is founded on national self-determination and resistance to outside military domination, so overriding an ally's government by troops contradicts it.

industrial-unions.rationale: Connolly's industrial unionism influenced one strand but it is not a general position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The 1916 Proclamation and Wolfe Tone's United Irishmen aimed to unite Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter.

religious-nation.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees religious and civil liberty and equal rights to all citizens.

defeat-communism.rationale: Republicans range from socialist to Catholic nationalist strands, so adherents are split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Adherents are split between the socialist strand and the nationalist strand that accepts the market.

socialized-care.rationale: The Democratic Programme promises child welfare and public care, but adherents are split on public services replacing family care.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees civil and religious liberty and republicans claim democratic rights, though armed groups used coercion historically.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees religious and civil liberty to all citizens and cherishes all children of the nation equally.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Irish republicanism is founded on rejecting British rule over Ireland, so governing a territory for another country's benefit is opposed.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Democratic Programme and Sinn Féin stress popular sovereignty and community voice, though direct participation in workplaces is not a main theme.

assisted-dying.rationale: Adherents are split and the tradition does not address it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Proclamation rests on the sovereign right of the people of Ireland to control their destinies, not on divine authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The tradition does not address this; adherents are split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Republicanism rejects monarchy and hereditary rule and rests on the sovereignty of the people.

property-franchise.rationale: The 1916 Proclamation guarantees universal suffrage to all Irish men and women, rejecting wealth qualifications.

reification.rationale: Republican sources do not take up the critique, and the socialist strand may agree while the nationalist strand would not.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees equal rights to all citizens and republicanism descends from Tone's union of Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees religious liberty and equal rights, and the tradition aims to unite faiths.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Republicanism aims to unite Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter, and the Proclamation promises equal rights regardless of difference.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Modern Sinn Féin works within the Good Friday Agreement's mandatory power-sharing institutions in Northern Ireland.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Democratic Programme makes the nation responsible for the welfare of children and the poor, implying public rather than charitable provision.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees equal rights and equal opportunities to all citizens and addresses 'Irishmen and Irishwomen' alike, implying equality within marriage.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Fianna Éireann and similar youth bodies were republican, but mainstream republicanism no longer backs drilled youth movements, so it is split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Democratic Programme subordinates private property to the public welfare and the right to work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Republicanism has combined armed struggle with politics, so disagreeing is the committed view.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Republican tradition honours the 1916 leaders and the dead of later struggles, as the Proclamation and its commemoration show.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees equal rights to all citizens, which cuts against majority control of the economy.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Strands differ: socialist republicans insist on working-class power while constitutional republicans stress popular sovereignty and the equal rights of all citizens.

municipal-property.rationale: The Democratic Programme vests the nation's resources in the people as a whole and favours co-operative industry, not community ownership by locality.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Older Sinn Féin policy (Éire Nua) proposed a federal Ireland, but the mainstream tradition aims at a single all-island republic; adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Proclamation invokes God and the tradition has deep Catholic roots, but modern republicanism is secular and strands are split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Republicans hold that the people are sovereign and resist Westminster's power to suspend devolved institutions, so revocable self-government sits poorly with the tradition.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees equal rights to all citizens, Tone aimed to unite Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter, and modern Sinn Féin is anti-racist, so organising by race is alien to it.

racial-pride.rationale: Irish national and cultural pride in ancestry is central to the tradition, although it is framed as nationhood rather than race.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Irish republicanism stresses a nation uniting Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter, with Irish language a cultural strand, but language is not what defines the nation in its core texts.

communal-electorates.rationale: The 1916 Proclamation guarantees religious and civil liberty and equal rights to all citizens, and the Tone tradition aims to unite Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter, which is opposed to sectarian electorates.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The 1919 Democratic Programme puts the nation's welfare above private property and the republican socialist strand (Connolly) is union-based.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Republicanism's religious stance is non-sectarian unity of Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter (Proclamation, Tone), not a view on whether religions share one truth; no inference beyond indifference.

workers-own-party.rationale: Connolly-line republicans favour a labour party, but mainstream Sinn Féin is a cross-class republican party, so adherents are split.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The 1916 Proclamation guarantees equal rights and opportunities to all citizens and addresses men and women alike, implying equal property rights.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not a historical republican issue; modern Sinn Féin backs climate action but without a stated trade-off against liberty, so no inference is possible.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees religious and civil liberty and equal rights to all, and cherishes all the nation's children equally.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Democratic Programme asks for social justice and the nation's ownership of its resources, so democracy is more than elections.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Proclamation grants the right of the people of Ireland to suffrage for all her men and women.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Adherents are split between a secular republican left and a Catholic nationalist tradition.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The 1919 Democratic Programme says the nation's soil belongs to the people and subordinates private property to public welfare.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees equal rights and opportunities to all citizens and addresses 'Irishmen and Irishwomen', and Sinn Féin stresses gender equality.

national-church-status.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees religious and civil liberty and equal rights to all, and the tradition seeks a secular republic not tied to one church.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Sinn Féin campaigns for a border poll under the Good Friday Agreement on Northern Ireland's constitutional future, though the tradition historically treated the island as one unit.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Proclamation guarantees religious and civil liberty and equal rights, and Tone's aim was to unite Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter, against denominational division.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Sinn Féin supports the liberal social positions on abortion and same-sex marriage, and the Proclamation promises equal rights to all citizens.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The Democratic Programme subordinates private property to the public welfare and the nation's wealth belongs to the people.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not a republican question; strands range from nationalist to socialist.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The Proclamation and Democratic Programme join national independence with cherishing all the nation's children equally.

material-over-identity.rationale: Modern Sinn Féin backs same-sex marriage, abortion access and the Irish language alongside economic policy.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The Democratic Programme committed to replacing the Poor Law with a native relief scheme, and Sinn Féin proposes expanded services. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A nation divided between states by a border drawn by an outside power should be reunified as one state.
missingStatements.rationale: Opposition to the partition of Ireland and the aim of a single Irish state is the defining republican position, pursued by constitutional and armed means.

notes: Dissident republicans and legitimists reject the Good Friday Agreement and would answer violence and institutions statements differently. The Democratic Programme's socialist content was diluted before adoption.
